subject: [Model Intake] CeruleanX-4b: compatibility checks + provisional pin request
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Model Intake] CeruleanX-4b: compatibility checks + provisional pin request

Hi team,

Product is pushing to onboard CeruleanX-4b (open checkpoint from DataWave partner) for a large-generation routing test next quarter. Attached are the model spec and a small sample of our expected request traces.

Top asks from Product & Solutions:
- Can infra + runtime confirm any known incompatibilities (tokenizer format, kv-cache layout, unsupported ops) with our current kernels?
- We'd like a provisional "pin" for the model family during the intake window so that we can run canaries without risk of automatic roll updates.
- If pinning is risky, propose the minimal variant set (e.g., quantized int8 vs. fp16) we should serve initially.

Constraints/warnings from Product: typical seq_len ~ 2048 for summarization flows; 3200 token bursts ~10% of traffic. Latency SLO is 250ms p50 on Dedicated.

Please treat this as time-sensitive: solutions is scheduling a demo with DataWave for May 14 and wants a clear go/no-go.

Thanks — I.

--
Irene Choi
Product Manager, Model Intake
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- ceruleanx-4b-specs.pdf (PDF)
- sample-workload-traces.csv (CSV)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Model Intake] CeruleanX-4b: compatibility checks + provisional pin request

Irene — thanks for the detail and the traces. Quick read: the model uses a nonstandard SentencePiece model with a few OOV tokens we haven't seen in our corpus. A couple of clarifying asks before we run formal checks:

1) Can you confirm the base sequence length the vendor trained on? (4k, 8k?)
2) Are you expecting to serve the full ckpt or a distilled variant?
3) For canary traffic can we limit bursts to 2% for the first 48 hours?

Initial notes from a quick tokenizer check (I ran local conversion): the vocab maps cleanly but there are 3 tokens that expand into long byte sequences which could inflate KV cache size for long-context sessions. If those coincide with the 3200 bursts we'll need to simulate memory pressure.

I'll spin up a compatibility job (tokenizer + forward pass smoke) but will need the full checkpoint link from DataWave or the quantized artifact from QuantCore.

—Aditya

--
Aditya Rao
Senior Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Model Intake] CeruleanX-4b: compatibility checks + provisional pin request

Looping in technical details from runtime side. Short version: we can support CeruleanX-4b but there are three things to decide before we pin:

- Kernel/Operator Coverage: vendor uses a custom fused attention op (attn_fast_v2). We don't have that kernel optimized for older Ampere boxes; fallback is to emulate with two kernels which increases latency 20-35% on p50 in our microbenchmarks.

- KV Cache Shape: because of the tokenizer expansion Aditya mentioned, effective KV cache per-request could push memory above our standard 16GB-per-GPU threshold for the smallest Dedicated SKU. That means either use a larger GPU SKU or limit max_context for canaries.

- Quantization Path: QuantCore provided an int8 artifact but uses a nonstandard calibration table. We need to validate logits parity (regression check) against fp16 on a sampled prompt set. If parity fails we should serve fp16 only and revisit.

Proposed immediate plan (can do within 6 business days):
1) Aditya to run tokenizer + forward smoke with vendor checkpoint (need link).
2) Runtime team will run microbenchmarks on 2xA100-40G and a 80GB test node to compare latency/memory.
3) If 80GB required for expected traffic, propose provisional pin to the 80GB variant with telemetry gating for 72 hours. Pin would be: model:ceruleanx-4b@v1.0-provisional (tags applied in model registry).
4) Add a telemetry set to capture token expansion ratio, p50/p95 latency, and OOMs.

If Product approves the canary percentage and SKU plan, we'll schedule the runs.

Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Model Intake] CeruleanX-4b: compatibility checks + provisional pin request

Thanks — this is actionable. I talked to Solutions about the demo cadence; Product can accept a provisional 80GB-only pin for the demo provided we: 

- Limit initial canary to 1% of traffic for 48 hours.
- Block bursts > 2048 tokens for canary traffic and have automatic fallback to S3-stored fp16 variant if telemetry shows >5% regression on quality/latency.

I've created a short intake card and added the acceptance criteria in the drive doc (link below). Karthik/Aditya: please post the microbenchmark results to INT-4123 and tag me.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Director, Model Operations
Redwood Inference

Irene/Laura — thanks for the quick coordination and the proposed plan. QuantCore has shared an int8 artifact with us; I'm CCing QuantCore sales to request the calibration metadata you mentioned.

For the May 14 demo, DataWave is fine with the 80GB pin and 1% canary as long as you share a short doc with expected p50 latency and any fallbacks we should communicate to our SREs. We can also provide a trimmed checkpoint (no optimizer state) if that helps speed the transfer.

Best,
Alice
